goal: The harness enforces a per-run cumulative cost ceiling: once total_cost_usd across all attempts reaches HarnessConfig.max_cost_usd, the run ends Status.FAILED (non-retryable) with a harness.budget_ceiling_breached event.

relevant: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/harness.py -- HarnessConfig (~line 310); the per-iteration cost rollup `attempt.total_cost_usd += cost` (~3196-3198) where the cumulative check belongs; the ABORT terminal path (~2111-2125, direct to Status.FAILED) the breach mirrors
packages/flywheel-core/tests/test_budget_ceilings.py -- the held-out oracle for this task; make it green, do not edit it
references: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/harness.py -- the ABORT path finalizes the attempt (Outcome.AGENT_ERROR) and transitions directly to Status.FAILED bypassing the retry arm; the budget breach reuses that shape (no new Outcome variant)
constraints: Add HarnessConfig.max_cost_usd: float = 0.0 (0 = unenforced, the fast default; back-compat).

The ceiling is PER-RUN cumulative: sum total_cost_usd across all attempts of the run (finalized attempts + the current one), checked after the per-iteration cost rollup and BEFORE grading, so a breach pre-empts the grade.

On breach: finalize the current attempt, emit a harness.budget_ceiling_breached telemetry event with payload {"ceiling": "cost_usd", "limit": <ceiling>, "observed": <run_total>}, and transition directly to Status.FAILED (terminal, non-retryable) mirroring the ABORT path.
Do not enforce max_tokens or wall_clock_seconds (out of scope); reuse Outcome.AGENT_ERROR for the breached attempt.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not thread the ceiling from flywheel.toml/policy -- that is sandbox-limit-threading.
Do not enforce token or wall-clock ceilings; do not add a new Outcome or Status variant.
Do not change behavior when max_cost_usd is 0 (the default); do not modify files under tests/ or weaken the held-out oracle or increment A/B oracles.
edge_cases: max_cost_usd=0.0 (default) never breaches, even at huge cost (back-compat with fast).
A breach in attempt 2 after attempt 1 failed validation must still fire (per-run accumulation across attempts), ending FAILED with two attempts.
The breach event fires before the grader runs -- a run that blew its budget does not pass.
